title: US tells election officials to be on guard against AI-powered tricks ahead of midterms
source_used: Reuters (text read in the Lufkin Daily News Reuters copy)
key_facts: The FBI and the US cyber defense agency CISA are urging election officials and the American public to be on guard against AI-powered tricks ahead of next month's midterm elections.
The alert was issued on Friday 16 Oct 2026 jointly by CISA and the FBI.
It says hackers may try to disrupt the midterm elections using bogus text messages and emails aimed at stealing passwords or other sensitive data.
It says election officials, candidates and their political organizations are attractive targets for malicious cyber criminals.
It says AI, which it calls 'super intelligence' (a term Reuters describes as Trump-approved), is allowing hackers to sharpen their rogue emails and texts so they look and sound more convincing.
quote_evidence: The FBI and the US cyber defense agency CISA are urging election officials -- and the American public -- to be on guard against AI-powered tricks ahead of next month's midterm elections.
An alert issued Friday by CISA and the FBI says that hackers may try to disrupt the midterm elections using bogus text messages and emails aimed at stealing passwords or other sensitive data.
why_it_matters_hint: Federal agencies are warning that AI makes phishing aimed at election staff and campaigns more convincing weeks before the vote.
notes: Reuters original (HTTP 401) not opened; the Reuters text is short and was read in the Lufkin Daily News copy (Reuters, Raphael Satter). The alert warns of a risk; the report names no specific attack. CISA stands for Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (expansion added by us). SEC would also fit as category; POL kept.
